svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop Learning Interface
svg.desc: A static SVG educational activity. Click word-bank labels to place them on the flower diagram. Use Hint, Check Answer, and Reset controls. Includes a pollination inset diagram.
svg.text: Interactive textbook lab · click labels to place · static SVG (no scripts)

g.text: Match each word-bank term to the dashed target slots. Arrows show anatomy leaders.
Read each dashed target slot around the flower.
Click a rounded label tile in the Word Bank.
It “snaps” into the matching anatomy slot (simulated drop).
Watch the leader arrow highlight the structure.
Use Hint, Check Answer, or Reset when ready.
Identify male (stamen) and female (pistil) parts and supporting floral organs used in pollination and seed formation.
Pollen moves from anther → stigma, then grows a tube down the style to the ovary.
4. Ovary develops into fruit; ovules → seeds
Word Bank — click a tile to place it on the diagram
Simulated drag-and-drop: each tile auto-snaps to its correct target. Place all 10, then open Check Answer.
Petal — colorful leaf-like part that attracts pollinators.
Sepal — outer green protection for the bud; together = calyx.
Stamen — male organ = filament + anther (produces pollen).
Pistil — female organ = stigma + style + ovary.
Receptacle — swollen stem tip that supports floral organs.
Anther — pollen-producing tip of the stamen.
Filament — stalk that holds up the anther.
Stigma — sticky top that receives pollen.
Style — tube connecting stigma to ovary.
Ovary — base containing ovules; becomes fruit after fertilization.
Stuck on male vs. female parts? Try this checklist:
The stamen is the male organ. Its stalk is the filament; its pollen tip is the anther (yellow pods).
The pistil is central: sticky stigma on top, style in the middle, ovary (with ovules) at the base.
Petals are large and pink for attraction. Sepals are greener and sit outside/beneath the petals. The receptacle is the green platform under everything.
Compare your placed tiles with the official matching key. Each term maps to one target:
Self-check: Did your arrows point to the
Petal — Often brightly colored; attracts insects/birds. Collection of petals = corolla.
Target A on the diagram (large pink structures).
Sepal — Protective outer segments of the flower bud. Collection of sepals = calyx.
Stamen — Male reproductive organ of the flower; composed of filament + anther.
Anther — Pollen-producing structure at the tip of a stamen (often bilobed).
Filament — Slender stalk that elevates the anther for pollen dispersal.
Pistil (carpel) — Female reproductive organ: stigma + style + ovary.
Stigma — Sticky apex that captures pollen grains during pollination.
Style — Neck through which a pollen tube grows toward the ovary.
Ovary — Basal chamber with ovules; develops into fruit after fertilization.
Receptacle — Expanded tip of the flower stalk that bears the floral organs.

svg.text: Static SVG learning interface · SMIL click-to-place · CSS :target popups · no JavaScript · no external assets
